resolvedQuestions.text: What does the SessionStart compact payload actually contain for a fork versus its parent session?
Where do fork sub-agent transcripts live, and do they carry the parent session_id or a distinct id?
Which hook paths (nudge, note-keep, claim, Stop-arm) key off session_id and therefore share the fork hazard?
What is the smallest correct fix that separates a fork from its parent without regressing the parent path?
What test or observable evidence would prove the fork misfire is gone?

keyFindings.text: The hook's only source gate is `payload.source !== 'compact'` plus a valid `payload.session_id`; nothing in the gate establishes that the caller is the top-level session, so any SessionStart with source=compact passes.
The hook is registered under SessionStart with an empty matcher, so it runs for every SessionStart source and relies entirely on that in-code source gate.

The parent session did not compact on 2026-10-21: its transcript holds six compact_boundary records, the last at 2026-10-20T16:19:05.871Z, and its last SessionStart:compact hook attachment is 2026-10-20T16:19:06.293Z.

All three 2026-10-21 fires executed inside fork sidechain transcripts, and each fork line matches its relaunch.log row to within ~30 ms: aea1c7f90bbedad3d at 14:44:41.466Z vs log 14:44:41.453Z, ae7668a35ed03d742 at 15:30:23.729Z vs log 15:30:23.714Z, a94347aac9778aa86 at 17:42:12.061Z vs log 17:42:12.039Z.

The fork's SessionStart payload carries the parent's session_id, because the hook logged sessionId=0b9dc60c-478f-4659-8191-2da52f1cd765 and resolved the parent's note while running inside the fork process.

Fork transcripts live at ~/.claude/projects/<project-slug>/<parent-session-id>/subagents/agent-<agentId>.jsonl with a sibling agent-<agentId>.meta.json, so the fork store is namespaced under the parent session id.
The fork marker exists on disk but never reaches the hook: agent-*.meta.json carries agentType=fork, isFork=true and spawnDepth=1, while the hook's gate reads only source and session_id.
The hook writes nudge state for the payload's session id before any fork-shaped guard, so a fork firing this path resets the parent's nudge level to 0 under the parent's own state filename.

The mechanism in one sentence: a fork inherits the parent's `session_id` and the platform emits `SessionStart` with `source: compact` inside it, so every session-keyed path resolves the parent's state while the hook's only gate is the very value the platform sets for a fork.

The hazard table: compact-pointer emits the parent's pointer and zeroes the parent's nudge level; session-prime injects the parent's compact brief and records a compaction boundary for the parent's session; spec-gate shares the parent's gate record; `claim` would accept a fork's claim of the parent's note; stop-arm and the PostToolUse nudge share the same keying but are not dispatched inside forks today.

The parent never compacted on 2026-10-21: six compact_boundary records exist, the last at 2026-10-20T16:19:05.871Z, and the parent transcript's last `SessionStart:compact` attachment is 2026-10-20T16:19:06.293Z, while three forks fired the pointer at 14:44, 15:30 and 17:42.

The fix is two clauses plus a reorder: emit only when the payload's transcript holds a compact_boundary strictly after the note's `created_at`, record one delivery per (note, boundary) so later fires for the same boundary stay silent, and move `writeState(sessionId, 0)` below every guard.

Four tests prove it: boundary-after-note emits and resets the level; no-boundary emits nothing and leaves the level intact; boundary-before-note emits nothing; a missing transcript emits nothing and logs `compact-pointer-skipped reason=no-transcript`.
The residual risk after the fix is a parent that compacts, ignores its own pointer and leaves the note open, which clause two covers by suppressing the repeat rather than by re-emitting it to a fork.

The fix does not depend on the one value still unproven locally, the fork's `transcript_path`, because the boundary guard behaves identically whether that path names the fork's transcript or the parent's.

The repo's own contract documents the Claude SessionStart payload as source (startup/compact/resume/clear), session_id, transcript_path, stop_hook_active and context_window_tokens — there is no agent id, subagent flag or fork marker any hook could read.

The contract states compact-pointer's intent as running on SessionStart "after a compaction", but the implementation trusts `source === 'compact'` as proof that a compaction happened, so the contract's precondition is unenforced in code.

A second, independent SessionStart hook in the same fork logged `SessionStart triggered (source: compact, session: 0b9dc60c-478f-4659-8191-2da52f1cd765)` to its stderr (recorded at line 195 of the fork transcript), independently confirming that a fork's payload carries source=compact and the parent's session id.

`session-prime`'s compact branch shares the hazard: it keys the cached compact brief by session_id and injects it whenever source=compact, so the same fork received the parent's post-compaction brief (cached at 2026-10-21T15:29:16.367Z) one minute before it read the parent's note.

Session-scoped hook state is broadly keyed by session_id rather than by agent: the spec-gate state directory holds one file per hex-encoded session id, and one of them decodes to 0b9dc60c-478f-4659-8191-2da52f1cd765, so a fork writing gate state writes the parent's record.

`openNotePathFor` selects a note by filename suffix `-<first 8 characters of session_id>.md` plus `status: open` and a frontmatter `session_id` match, so a fork carrying the parent's session id resolves the parent's open note and no agent check exists anywhere on that path.

The only guard that could have suppressed the fork fire, `handoffPending`, returns false unless `SKILLED_LOOP_ID` is set, and the parent's note carries an empty `loop_id:` because prepare ran outside the wrapper, so the guard short-circuits and the pointer is emitted.

`seedText({ afterCompaction: true })` asserts "This session was compacted after it wrote a handoff note", a false claim when the emitter is a fork that never compacted, and it produces exactly the claim invocation the two fork replies refused.

The hook calls `writeState(sessionId, 0)` before any fork-shaped guard, and `stateFilePath` builds `nudge-<session>.json` from the payload session id, so each fork fire rewrites the parent's own nudge ladder to level 0 — the parent then nudges again sooner than its real context fill warrants.

`claimHandoff` validates only that the supplied session id is well formed and that the note is open; it never compares the caller's session against the note's `session_id`, so a fork passing `--session <parent>` would have claimed the parent's note successfully and marked it claimed.

Note identity is only eight characters of session id, so the note lookup's own filter is coarser than the note's full session identity — a second session whose id shares those eight characters would match the same note.

The platform fires a dedicated `SubagentStart` event whose matcher is `fork` inside sub-agents — 3, 8 and 6 occurrences in the 14:44, 15:30 and 17:42 forks — so fork-ness is observable at the platform level even though the SessionStart payload itself carries no fork field.
The project's SessionStart adapters do run inside forks: session-prime, worktree-guard, check-git-hooks, git-live-follow and compact-pointer all produced hook_success entries in the fork transcripts.

The project's PostToolUse `context-nudge` and Stop `stop-arm` adapters produced no attachment at all in any of the three forks; the only PostToolUse entries were the Orca agent-hook bridge, so the fork hazard is confined to SessionStart dispatch plus whatever the injected seed makes the model do.

Every hook attachment inside a fork carries `agentId` and `isSidechain: true` on the transcript record itself, so the fork's identity is provable from the transcript while it is absent from the payload the adapter receives.

`worktree-guard` announced "This top-level session is running on the shared 'main' checkout" inside a fork, a second adapter that assumes it is addressing a top-level session — evidence the assumption is family-wide rather than one hook's bug.

`context-nudge` needs only `session_id` and `transcript_path` and writes state under the payload session id exactly as compact-pointer does, so if PostToolUse dispatch ever reaches forks the same parent-state overwrite appears there too.

`stop-arm` gates its arm path on `SKILLED_LOOP_ID`, requires `payload.transcript_path`, and hands that path to the killer it spawns, so if Stop dispatch ever reached a fork the killer would watch a fork transcript while arming the parent's loop record.

`context-nudge` derives the fill ratio from `payload.transcript_path` and persists the level under `payload.session_id`, the same parent-state write compact-pointer performs at level 0 — the difference is only which level it writes.

No local record of a fork's `transcript_path` exists: a search of the Claude state tree outside the project transcripts found no stored `subagents/agent-` path, so neither a fork's own jsonl nor the parent transcript can be confirmed as the value a fork's payload carries.

The parent transcript contains zero sidechain records, so a fork never writes its turns into the parent file; the fork transcript and the parent transcript are disjoint files, which means a transcript-based check reads exactly one of them and never a blend.

`readClaudeFill` already filters `entry.isSidechain !== true`, so the repo's transcript reader was written expecting sidechain entries to be possible in a transcript it reads — the notion that a transcript can contain fork turns already exists in the code, but no reader exposes it to the compact path.

The adapter harness already supports a transcript per payload through `writeTranscript`, so a compaction-evidence guard can be tested without new fixtures; the payload factory also omits `transcript_path`, which makes the missing-path branch explicitly testable.

The evidence to require is a record with `type: system`, `subtype: compact_boundary` and a `timestamp`; the parent transcript carries six such records and none on 2026-10-21, while a fork's SessionStart implies a compaction that never wrote one.

The fix is a guard ahead of the emit: emit only when the transcript named by the payload holds a compact_boundary at or after the note's `created_at`, which suppresses every fork fire observed and every future one whose transcript lacks a boundary.

`writeState(sessionId, 0)` currently runs before the guards, so a suppressed fire would still reset the parent's nudge ladder; moving the reset below the guards makes suppression side-effect free, and the existing emitting-path test still passes.

Treating a missing `transcript_path` as "cannot verify" is the honest branch, and it should fail closed with its own log row so a real parent regression becomes visible in `relaunch.log` rather than silent.

`session-prime` needs the same gate or the fork still receives the parent's cached compact brief; its cache is keyed by session id and validated only for a 30-minute TTL and payload semantics, both of which a fork satisfies.

`compact-pointer` exists only in the Claude adapter — there is no codex, pi, hermes or opencode equivalent — so the fix is one adapter plus its tests, and the pointer's own blast radius is Claude-only.

Fail-closed on a missing transcript is the asymmetric choice: a wrong emission injects a false "you were compacted" and can get the parent's note claimed, while a wrong suppression only withholds a reminder whose note stays open and reclaimable.

Fail-closed changes the meaning of the existing emitting test, which passes a payload with no transcript at all; the fix must extend the payload factory to carry a transcript that holds a boundary, so the emitting path stays covered rather than silently deleted.

`session-prime` forwards the payload's source to the directive-lifecycle store as `{session_id, boundary}`, so a fork's SessionStart(source=compact) records a compaction boundary against the parent's session id in a second subsystem.

Every one of these writes is keyed by session_id, so a fork can silently rewrite the parent's nudge level, its directive boundary and its gate state; no part of the SessionStart family records which agent performed the write.
No code in the hooks tree or the spec-kit runtime reads a `compact_boundary` record today, so the guard needs a new small reader and cannot borrow correctness from an existing tested one.

`latestTailEntry` is private to `context-usage.cjs` and not exported, so a boundary reader either exports that helper or reads the transcript tail on its own — the cheaper option is a dedicated tail scan in the relaunch lib.

Test A (boundary newer than the note): payload `{hook_event_name: 'SessionStart', source: 'compact', session_id, transcript_path}` where the transcript holds a boundary after the note's `created_at`; expects the compacted-session context and the claim command, and expects the nudge file reset to `{level:0}`.

Test B (boundary absent — the reproduced fork case): the same payload with a transcript that has no boundary; expects empty stdout and the nudge file still `{level:2}`, which is the regression test for the observed misfire and for the side-effect reorder.
Test C (stale boundary): a boundary timestamped before the note's `created_at`; expects empty stdout, because a compaction that predates the note cannot be the one that lost the note's detail.
Test D (missing transcript): no `transcript_path` in the payload; expects empty stdout and a `compact-pointer-skipped reason=no-transcript` row in `relaunch.log`, so a silent disable is impossible.

The harness needs one new fixture helper that writes a transcript containing a `{"type":"system","subtype":"compact_boundary","timestamp":...}` record, because `writeTranscript` emits a single assistant record with no timestamp control.

Residual window A: when the parent genuinely compacts after writing a note and never claims it, every later fork still finds a boundary and still receives the parent's pointer, so the boundary guard narrows the failing class rather than closing it.

Residual window B: a boundary and a note created within the same second make ordering ambiguous, and a "boundary at or after the note" comparison resolves that ambiguity in the fork's favour, so the guard should require the boundary to be strictly after the note's `created_at`.

A second, equally small clause closes window A: record one delivery per (note path, boundary timestamp) in the relaunch state directory and skip a repeat, which suppresses the second and third fork fires while letting the parent's next genuine compaction re-arm the pointer.

The delivery marker must be its own state file rather than a field inside `nudge-<session>.json`, because the existing emitting test asserts that file deep-equals `{level:0}` and widening the record would break that assertion without adding coverage.

A compact cache for the parent session existed with `cachedAt` 2026-10-21T15:29:16.367Z while the parent transcript carries no record at 15:29 at all and no boundary on 2026-10-21, so the presence of a compact cache is not evidence that a compaction happened.

The `writeState(sessionId, 0)` reorder is required whichever clause lands: without it every suppressed fork fire still resets the parent's ladder, so the suppression would be visible only in stdout and invisible in state.

ruledOutDirections.text: "The parent compacted and the transcript simply lacks the boundary": ruled out because the parent transcript has zero compact_boundary records on 2026-10-21 while three SessionStart:compact hook attachments exist only in fork sidechains.
"The hook is mis-registered on a start source other than compact": ruled out because the registration has an empty matcher and the hook returns early unless `payload.source === 'compact'`.

"Disable the pointer for all forks by registering a SubagentStart marker": ruled out as the smallest fix, because it adds a new hook registration where a transcript check inside the existing hook suffices.
"Add an agent-identity check to the payload": ruled out for the third time by the documented payload contract, which carries no agent field.
"The fork ran the hook in a different state directory": ruled out because the hook's `stateDir()` keys on uid (501), not on agent, so forks and parent share one relaunch state directory.
"Read the fork marker out of the payload": ruled out by the documented payload contract, which exposes no agent or fork field. Any fix must derive fork-ness from a value the payload does carry.
"The pending-handoff guard covers the unwrapped case": ruled out because the guard is keyed on `SKILLED_LOOP_ID` and the observed note has an empty `loop_id`.

"The fork is protected because a model refuses the instruction": ruled out as a control, since `claimHandoff` would have accepted the claim; the refusals observed were model judgment, not an enforced guarantee.
"The fork hazard can be detected from transcript-side metadata by the hook": ruled out because `agentId`/`isSidechain` live on transcript records, while the adapter only receives the payload.

"Every project hook misfires in a fork": ruled out by the attachment census — PostToolUse and Stop adapters never ran in the forks, so the blast radius is SessionStart plus the seed's instruction, not the whole hook surface.

"Key the fix on transcript_path matching a `/subagents/` segment": not refuted, but unprovable from local evidence, and it would be wrong if the payload names the parent transcript. Recorded as a candidate with a known risk rather than the recommendation.
"Fork writes its turns into the parent transcript, so one path covers both": ruled out by the zero sidechain count in the parent transcript.
"Infer compaction from the nudge state file": ruled out because the state file is exactly what the hook overwrites, so it cannot serve as evidence.
"Patch only the seed text so it stops claiming a compaction": ruled out as insufficient, because the fork would still be pushed to claim the parent's note; the text is a symptom of the missing gate.

"Fail open on a missing transcript to protect the parent path": ruled out because the parent path is documented to carry `transcript_path`, and a silent fail-open reproduces exactly the observed misfire.
"Apply the same fix to every runtime adapter": ruled out because no other runtime has a compact pointer; the shared hazard is session-keyed state, which is a different finding with a different fix.
"Assert on the log row alone": ruled out as the primary evidence, because a log row proves a decision was recorded, not that the parent path still emits.
"Reuse the existing transcript reader": ruled out because nothing in the tree parses compaction boundaries and the tail helper is not exported.
"The boundary guard alone is sufficient": ruled out by residual window A, which the guard structurally cannot see.
"Store the delivery marker in the note frontmatter": ruled out because the note is the parent's artifact and the marker would then travel with it into a future claim, confusing `status` semantics.
